summary: The newest material Flow event regressed from distinct provider-query temporal witnesses to one shared retrieval interval for four separately returned observations: Bybit spot, Bybit linear, Twelve Data, and Bybit orderbook all use 2026-10-07T14:31:45.699Z–14:31:47.748Z. The three Massive futures calls likewise share one 46-second interval without a batch_capture_id or request-membership record. Independent fresh queries reproduced every 13:00 UTC BTC statistic exactly, so the market anomaly is not falsified; however, per-response availability timing remains unauditable. This is the second documented recurrence after run-local recovery, proving the repair is not a durable scientific gate.
surface: icarus-mcp event/evidence contract and validator coverage

evidence.finding: Bybit spot, Bybit linear, Twelve Data, and Bybit orderbook all carry the identical retrieval interval 14:31:45.699Z–14:31:47.748Z. No batch_capture_id, per-request interval, or request-membership list is persisted. NQZ6/GCZ6/SIZ6 similarly share one aggregate interval.

The exact-read-back receipt repeats the shared intervals while claiming preserved clocks; completed-bar ends are present and precede the batch interval, but individual response availability is not attested.
The earlier regression defined unexplained shared timestamps as insufficient and required either distinct per-request intervals or an explicit batch capture identity and membership list.
The intervening recovery was verified because each provider query had a distinct interval; it explicitly warned that no validator or contract gate made the repair durable.

Fresh sequential provider queries exactly reproduced the 13:00 UTC metrics: spot range $789.60 z +4.5517, volume 935.869759 BTC z +3.7803; linear range $861.30 z +4.7172, volume 8427.112 BTC z +5.5683; Twelve Data range $764.76 z +4.1604.

evidence.query: GitHub code search on main for retrieved_at_start_utc, completed_bar_end_utc, and batch_capture_id
evidence.finding: Search results contain evidence artifacts only; batch_capture_id appears solely in the prior regression event. No implementation or test path enforcing per-request witnesses or explicit batch semantics was found.
The active v1 contract still does not require per-query retrieval intervals, completed-bar witnesses, batch identity, request membership, or causal-order validation.

The shared interval likely describes a parallel query batch, but without persisted request membership or individual completion times it cannot prove when each provider response became available. Raw connector logs remain unavailable.

conflicts: The BTC range and volume statistics are independently reproducible and remain usable as numerical observations.
Completed-bar end 14:00 UTC precedes the shared 14:31 interval, so broad causal ordering is plausible; the defect is loss of per-response temporal attestation, not backdating evidence.
A batch interval could be scientifically acceptable only with an explicit batch_capture_id and complete request-membership semantics, which are absent.
limitations: Raw connector invocation logs and monotonic-clock attestations were unavailable.
No claim is made that the BTC anomaly itself is numerically wrong.
No scheduler, contract, code, test, deployment, or trading change was authorized.
required_remediation: Version the event/evidence contract to require retrieved_at_start_utc and retrieved_at_end_utc per provider response, plus completed_bar_end_utc for completed-bar claims.
Permit shared intervals only when an explicit batch_capture_id, batch start/end, and complete request-membership list are persisted.
Implement a validator enforcing completed_bar_end <= retrieval start <= retrieval end <= assertion time and rejecting unexplained shared witnesses.
Retain the prior regression, recovery, latest regression, and this independent oracle as negative/positive/negative fixtures.
next_independent_verification_target: Audit and test the Flow event-construction path. Durable clearance requires an automatic validator to reject the 14:31 artifact shape while accepting distinct per-request intervals or an explicitly identified parallel batch.

daedalus.finding: The newest material Flow artifact preserves broad ordering but regresses from distinct provider-query intervals to unexplained shared batch intervals.

aegis.finding: Independent per-response availability timing is unavailable for four BTC observations and three futures queries; the same defect has now recurred after two run-local recoveries.
